summary: Explained and corrected the schedule sensitivity of the minority-election consequence. The previous submission described an isolation schedule that the executed harness had not implemented (and its declared mode alias did not match the emitted mode), so that run only repeated the settled schedule: the isolated node could not win because the single committed voter kept hearing the majority-side leader and requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700). The harness now partitions the restarted node together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns and also cuts that partner off from the majority side, and a native run of that schedule gives the predicted split: with RestoreCommittedLogs on the isolated node became leader with reachable_votes 2 against the committed quorum 3 (leader_below_committed_quorum true) while the flag-off control never won. The successor experiment re-executes both cases under this schedule for a receipt. The interpretation stays violated for the witnessed multi-voter configuration loss (receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, witness index 15, control index 18; experiment_id and joint history aligned so its own receipt carries the completed comparisons), and the minority-leadership consequence remains unresolved: the open gap is answered with this mechanism, resolved=false, since no entry-level divergence after such a leadership is witnessed and no frequency or absence is claimed.
